# Results — Study 155 (Asset-Turnover) on real EDGAR panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py).  One recipe — annual quintile sort on
Revenues / Assets (asset turnover) from fiscal year y, go long the top quintile, measure
calendar-year y+1 returns vs the equal-weight universe — run on the shared EDGAR cache for the
current S&P 500 members.  As-of **2026-06-14**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Concept | Fiscal years | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| EDGAR cache | Revenues | 2007–2026 | `da1c8de15999` |
| EDGAR cache | Assets | 2006–2026 | `4b8191daaf52` |
| EDGAR cache | NetIncomeLoss | 2007–2026 | `ad9d6dd0219a` |
| EDGAR cache | \_edgar\_yrret (annual returns) | 1962–2026 | `334fef9f1e42` |

**Signal window**: fiscal years 2008–2023 (16 annual observations; forward returns 2009–2024).
**Universe**: current S&P 500 members projected backwards (survivorship-biased).
**Coverage**: 95–264 firms with valid AT and return data per year (median ~210).

> **SURVIVORSHIP-BIAS CAVEAT**: the EDGAR cache covers only firms in the *current* S&P 500
> projected backwards — every company in the panel survived to 2026.  All results are upper bounds
> on the true live effect.  A real implementation would include firms that were subsequently delisted
> or went bankrupt, which would reduce the measured excess return.  Report all numbers with this
> caveat in mind.

## The honest test — top-quintile excess vs equal-weight market

Signal: AT = Revenues / Assets (fiscal year y), winsorised at the 99th cross-sectional percentile.
Portfolio: equal-weight top quintile vs equal-weight universe.  Reporting lag: signal at y → returns
at y+1 (conservative one-year lag beyond filing deadline).

| Portfolio | Mean (%/yr) | Sharpe | HAC *t* | Hit rate | n years |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Top quintile (high AT)** | **+19.5%** | **1.49** | **+9.64** | **94%** | **16** |
| Equal-weight market | +18.3% | 1.36 | +8.96 | 88% | 16 |
| **Excess (top − market)** | **+1.3%** | **0.28** | **+1.31** | **62%** | **16** |
| Bottom quintile (low AT) | +15.6% | 0.88 | +5.41 | 81% | 16 |
| Long-short (top − bottom) | +3.9% | 0.55 | +2.36 | 69% | 16 |

HAC *t* = **+1.31** on the top-quintile hedge — **not distinguishable from zero** at the 2.0 bar.
And this is already the survivorship-biased upper bound: the true *t* in a properly specified live
universe would be lower.  Verdict: **NONE**.

The **long-short** (top minus bottom quintile) clears the bar at *t* = +2.36, driven mainly by
the **bottom quintile lagging**, not the top quintile showing genuine alpha.

## Head-to-head: AT vs ROA (the independence test)

The same quintile sort run on NetIncomeLoss / Assets (ROA) in the same years and universe.

| Signal | Hedge mean | Sharpe | HAC *t* | Hit rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| AT (Revenues / Assets) | +1.3%/yr | 0.28 | +1.31 | 62% |
| ROA (NetIncomeLoss / Assets) | −0.2%/yr | −0.03 | −0.13 | 44% |
| **AT minus ROA (incremental)** | **+1.4%/yr** | — | **+1.76** | — |

ROA shows **no robust top-quintile premium** on this panel (HAC *t* = −0.13).  AT's incremental
contribution over ROA is +1.4%/yr with *t* = +1.76 — not significant at the 2.0 bar.

Neither metric produces a robust standalone long-only premium in this survivorship-biased S&P 500
sample.  The apparent "DuPont efficiency premium" that appears in some academic papers does not
replicate here on the top quintile in isolation.

## Random portfolio control

500 random draws of the same quintile size per year vs equal-weight market:
- Mean random excess: −0.1%/yr (Std: 5.0%)
- AT top quintile beats 65% of random draws

The 65% figure suggests mild separation from randomness, but well below the level that would
confirm a robust signal — and the survivorship bias inflates even this number.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Top-quintile excess **+1.3%/yr**, HAC *t* = **+1.31** (16 annual
  observations) — not distinguishable from zero.  This is a survivorship-biased upper bound;
  the true live *t* is lower.  ROA also shows no robust top-quintile premium (*t* = −0.13).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Annual rebalance, concentrated ~40-name portfolio, no robust
  signal, and the whole panel is survivorship-biased — any positive number is a ceiling.
- **Adds over ROA? — NO.** Incremental +1.4%/yr (*t* = +1.76) — not significant.
  Neither AT nor ROA produces a standalone robust premium in this universe.
- **The one significant number**: the long-short (*t* = +2.36), driven mainly by the
  bottom quintile lagging — a shorting requirement, not a long-only premium.
